correctness.rationale: The greedy output is always independent and maximal. For any point set A, maximality forces exactly the lines disjoint from A, and they must cover the omitted points. The Fano incidence rules give the listed five types: triples on a line leave no disjoint line, and noncollinear triples leave one disjoint line and one uncovered omitted point. A specified independent output occurs iff every outside vertex has an earlier neighbor in the output: the first accepted outside vertex would otherwise require an earlier rejected selected neighbor, impossible without a still earlier accepted outside vertex. For a selected-site ordering with exclusion counts f_i, the exponential-time gaps integrate to the reciprocal of the product of the suffix sums of 1+f_i; this agrees with all nine ordered simplex certificate rows. Independently, an integer dynamic program over (seen, accepted) masks extended each permutation prefix by each unseen vertex, with the graph built as the nonzero binary triples and their two-dimensional subspaces. At layer k the total count is (14)_k; at k=14, division by 14! gives the exact probabilities of all 37 outputs. It reproduced all type multiplicities, per-output probabilities, terminal law and fifteen prefix means, and checked total variation, amplification and the density difference exactly. Given k independent exponential arrivals by t the order is a uniform prefix, which proves the Bernstein mixture including t=0 and saturation. On the infinite cubic tree a branch-root vacancy q(t) obeys q'=-e^(-t) q², so the full-root terminal occupation is the integral of (1+p)^(-3) from p=0 to 1, namely 3/8.
residual_risks: Exact enumeration concerns this fourteen-vertex graph only. The finite-time law claimed is the mean, not the entire finite-time state distribution.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a natural cubic girth-six benchmark for comparing graph cycles with the infinite-tree RSA baseline. The exact weights expose the kinetic bias that an independence polynomial or an average alone misses: the maximum sets are selected about 6.34 times as often as under uniform maximal-set sampling, with total variation 293/777. The full finite-time mean gives a reproducible benchmark for simulations or analytic approximations on the cage, not an arbitrary cutoff or an extrapolated extremal claim.
residual_risks: The comparison to the cubic tree is a finite-graph benchmark; it does not establish behavior of other cages or extremality among cubic graphs.
